subject: Ratecard transparency and line-item usage export for commit discussion
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Ratecard transparency and line-item usage export for commit discussion

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Nimbus’ production traffic profile and multi-model mix make this a great candidate for a committed tier to get predictable unit economics. Before we finalize a proposal, could you share two things so we can map pricing to your invoice structure:  

1) A simple CSV (one month preferred) with line-level usage by date, model name (or model family), prompt vs completion tokens, and route/operation (chat/generate/embeddings).
2) Any current contract language or invoice samples that show how you map usage to line items (we want to ensure the ratecard maps 1:1 to your finance system).

To be clear on Redwood’s side: we typically propose a three-tier commit (50k / 250k / 1M token slabs) with volume discounts and an overage credit mechanism for sustained overrun months. We can tailor slabs as needed based on your traffic shape.

If you can send the CSV and a sample invoice, we’ll return a redlined ratecard and a sample mapping document showing exactly how each line item will appear on your monthly invoice. Attaching a short checklist of the fields that are most helpful for our billing engineers.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: billing_field_checklist.txt (one-line list of required CSV columns)

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbus.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ratecard transparency and line-item usage export for commit discussion

Alex —

Thanks — attaching one month of export (Nimbus_Usage_Summary_202709.csv). It includes date, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, request_type (chat/generate/embed), and project tag. I redacted a few internal project names.

Two quick clarifications:  
- We run both open and proprietary variants; can you break out per-model SKU pricing?
- Our finance team needs a sample invoice view that shows how committed discounts and overage credits will appear.

Tom (cc) will own the finance side — looping him in for any mapping questions. We’ll also route any contract changes through legal.

–Sara
SVP of Product, Nimbus AI

Attachment: Nimbus_Usage_Summary_202709.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Ratecard transparency and line-item usage export for commit discussion

Team —

I pulled Sara’s CSV and did a quick pivot. High-level observations:
- ~72% of tokens are completions, and 60% of spend maps to two LLM families (r-lm-xl, r-lm-base).
- They have consistent weekday peaks that make a reserved buffer + burst policy plausible.
- Their tagging is decent; mapping should be straightforward.

Proposed approach for reply:
1) Provide per-model SKU price table (hosted rates + committed slab discounts).
2) Include a sample invoice PDF mock that shows: gross charges, commit discount applied, overage credits, prorations.
3) Offer a short pilot amendment (60 days) for them to validate line-item granularity with their finance export.

I drafted a proposed ratecard (Redwood_Proposed_Ratecard_20270914.pdf). I recommend offering a 12% discount at the 250k slab and 20% at 1M, with a 90% carry-forward credit for sustained monthly overages.

—Lauren
Director, Revenue Operations

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Ratecard_20270914.pdf

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbus.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Ratecard transparency and line-item usage export for commit discussion

Sara / Tom —

Appreciate the CSV. Per Lauren’s analysis, attached is a concise proposal that includes:  
- Per-model hosted SKU table (shows open vs proprietary variants and the correspondent per-token base rate).
- Proposed commit slabs and the discount schedule.
- Sample invoice mock (two pages) that mirrors your current line-item columns — demonstrates how discounted line items & overage credits will show up.
- A short 60-day pilot amendment if you want to validate the export-to-invoice flow before a 12-month commit.

We’re also including a DocuSign link for an amendment if you want to move quickly (link in the attachments file). If legal needs different wording for invoice visibility or audit logs, point them to our compliance pack and we’ll loop Security.

Next steps:
- Tom: please confirm that the sample invoice structure satisfies Nimbus finance (I can share a mapping CSV).
- Sara: any model-specific SPLs you want us to price differently?

If you confirm, I can have our billing engineer share a line-by-line mapping (CSV) that your AP system can ingest.

Best,
Alex
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Amendment_DocuSign_Link.txt (DocuSign link and short instruction)

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbus.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbus.ai>
Cc: legal@nimbus.ai, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ratecard transparency and line-item usage export for commit discussion

Alex/Sara —

Reviewed the sample invoice mock. This looks good from our AP perspective; two small asks before we sign:  
1) Can Redwood add an export flag column (invoice_line_id) in the mapping CSV so our system can reconcile each usage row to the invoice line?
2) Legal wants a line in the amendment that Redwood will provide the raw per-request KV cache identifiers and audit log access for any line-item disputes for 6 months after invoice generation.

If you’re able to commit those two items, we can route the amendment through legal this week and get procurement to sign. I’ll coordinate with our legal alias (legal@nimbus.ai).

Thanks — Tom
Head of Finance, Nimbus AI

On Thu, Sep 16, 2027 at 09:12 AM Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Tom — we can add invoice_line_id in the mapping CSV.
> Regarding audit logs: we provide per-request metadata and a 6-month retention option for billing disputes as part of our Private/Enterprise package. I’ll have Security prepare the specific wording for the amendment.
> 
> I’ll generate the mapping CSV and update the DocuSign amendment accordingly.
> 
> —Alex
